content.user_title: Build and Fix Britecharts v3 Charts
content.value_statement: Britecharts charts can fail when code uses outdated APIs, incorrect data fields, or misplaced tooltips. This skill guides chart implementation and migration with specific v3 examples for JavaScript, React, and framework wrappers.
actual_capabilities: Select chart types and map input records to the documented Britecharts v3 data fields.
Write vanilla JavaScript chart setup with stylesheet imports, explicit sizing, redraws, and loading states.
Configure chart-specific tooltip attachment points, event handlers, and label mappings.
Compose React charts with Tooltip, ResponsiveContainer, immutable data updates, and export controls.
Integrate framework wrappers through create, update, and destroy lifecycle methods with typed configuration guidance.
Guide v2 migrations covering package imports, line data, removed accessors, formatting, and React behavior.
limitations: Targets Britecharts v3, not ongoing maintenance of v2 APIs or unrelated chart libraries.
Requires the chart packages, stylesheet, and a suitable application environment; the skill does not bundle the chart runtime.
Provides implementation guidance and examples, not an automated chart validation or browser testing service.
Older browsers require separate ES2020 transpilation; CDN examples also require network access and trust in external dependencies.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: integrate a chart into an existing React dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a chart module
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this Britecharts v2 module to v3: [module]. Preserve exports and explain changes to dependencies, data shapes, removed accessors, and tooltip wiring.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: upgrade existing chart code while preserving its application contract.

output_examples.input: My v3 line chart still receives nested v2 series data and renders incorrectly.
output: Flatten the nested series into individual points inside the required data wrapper.
Repeat the series label and numeric identifier on every point, alongside its ISO date and value.
Replace removed accessors and confirm the stylesheet is imported.

output_examples.input: My React stacked bar chart does not resize, and its tooltip series colors are missing.
output: Use ResponsiveContainer to supply the chart width.
Configure Tooltip to read series names from the stack field.
Pass the tooltip render props to StackedBar and replace data objects when values change.

output_examples.input: How should a Vue component manage a Britecharts chart?
output: Create the chart after the container mounts and retain the returned chart instance.
Update that instance when data or configuration changes.
Destroy the chart when the component unmounts.

best_practices: Check installed package names and confirm the project targets v3 before choosing imports or accessors.
Match chart data fields exactly and consult the chart reference before adding configuration options.
Import the stylesheet once, measure container width, and verify tooltip behavior after the first draw.
anti_patterns: Reusing removed v2 accessors or nested line data without migration.
Mutating React chart data in place and expecting a redraw.
Attaching every tooltip to the same element or omitting chart-specific field mappings.

faq.question: Which Britecharts version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers v3 and includes migration guidance for projects using the older britecharts or britecharts-react packages.

faq.question: Can I use it without React?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers vanilla JavaScript through core and lifecycle wrappers for frameworks such as Vue, Svelte, and Angular.

faq.question: Does the skill install the chart libraries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents npm installation commands and CDN examples; installation still requires execution in your project environment.

faq.question: Why does a chart appear black or unstyled?
faq.answer: The required Britecharts stylesheet may be missing. The skill shows its import path and recommends importing it once.

faq.question: Does it cover responsive charts and accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents container sizing, React responsiveness, accessible titles, built-in data tables, keyboard navigation, and color palettes.

faq.question: Will it verify every generated chart in a browser?
faq.answer: No. It provides API guidance and a review checklist, but application-specific testing and visual verification remain necessary.
